cases.case_name: National Seeds Corporation vs M.Madhusudhan Reddy
cases.summary: - Farmers purchased seeds from National Seeds Corporation - Seeds showed poor germination (60% vs expected 90%+) - Uneven plant height (3-6 feet), irregular flowering - Expected yield 600-700 kg/acre, actual 150-200 kg/acre - Claims rejected; farmers approached Consumer Forums NSCL ARGUED: - Seeds Act 1966 is special legislation; Consumer Forums lack jurisdiction - Farmers are not "consumers" - purchased for commercial purpose - Section 13(1)(c) not followed - no laboratory testing of samples -
cases.key_holding: 1. Consumer Forums have jurisdiction - Seeds Act and Consumer Act operate in different spheres 2. Farmers are "consumers" - seeds purchased for earning livelihood, not resale 3. Section 13(1)(c) strict compliance not mandatory - expecting farmers to retain samples unrealistic 4. Arbitration clause n
legal_principles: Farmers entitled to compensation under Consumer Protection Act for defective seeds causing crop failure. Special regulatory legislation does not exclude consumer protection remedies.

cases.case_name: Ebix Singapore vs Committee of Creditors of Educomp
cases.judges: Justice M.R. Shah & Justice D.Y. Chandrachud
cases.summary: Three consolidated appeals: 1. EBIX: Sought withdrawal citing fraud investigations, delays (27 months) 2. KUNDAN CARE: Sought withdrawal citing PPA termination, equipment damage 3. SEROCO: Sought modification reducing payment due to COVID-19 APPLICANTS ARGUED: - Resolution plan not binding until Section 31 NCLT approval - Six-month validity clause expired - Material non-disclosure by Resolution Professional - Changed commercial circumstances - NCLT has inherent powers under Section 60(5) COC ARG
cases.key_holding: 1. NO UNILATERAL WITHDRAWAL POST-COC APPROVAL "Successful Resolution Applicant does not have right to withdraw after CoC approval"
legal_principles: Resolution plans create binding obligations once CoC approves. No unilateral withdrawal permitted absent statutory provision. Protects creditors, enforces timelines, upholds process sanctity.

cases.case_name: Vijay Prakash vs UOI (Privacy and RTI)
cases.summary: - Former IAF officer sought wife's (DRDO employee) service records under RTI - Wife posted at 4 AFSB Varanasi; matrimonial dispute pending - Requested leave forms, DSOP nominations, investment records - Information denied citing Section 8(1)(j) - personal information exemption
cases.key_holding: 1. Privacy is fundamental right - cannot be forfeited by becoming public servant 2. Public servants entitled to privacy for personal information unrelated to official duties 3. "Public interest" cannot be presumed merely because subject is government employee 4. Burden on information seeker to estab
legal_principles: Personal information of public servants protected unless specific public interest demonstrated regarding accountability/performance of official duties.
